current_answer: CodeSupply is open to 3 November 2026 at 12:00 CET. NLnet first checks eligibility, then weights relevance and impact at 40%, technical feasibility at 30%, and value for money at 30%. A score above 5.0/7 advances a proposal to further review, not to an award.

catalogue_card.question: Would your CodeSupply proposal pass the first review?
catalogue_card.text: Check project fit and European dimension first. NLnet then weights relevance and impact at 40%, technical feasibility at 30%, and value at 30%; above 5.0/7 only advances you to the next stage.

summary: CodeSupply’s first call still closes 3 November 2026 at 12:00 CET for eligible open-source software-supply-chain work.
Hard eligibility precedes weighted scoring. The issuer gives relevance and impact the largest share, 40%.
A first request may be EUR 5,000–50,000, but neither an open form nor a qualifying score guarantees funding.
uncertainty: The public guide cannot score or approve a particular proposal.
The issuer does not publish an applicant-specific award or payment date; first-party analytics and applicant outcomes are unavailable.
freshness_note: CodeSupply call, form and selection guide verified 28 October 2026. Other catalogue rows retain their own check dates.
